name: vanilla-responsive-ui
description: Dependency-free, accessible (WCAG 2.2 AA), responsive UI components, layouts and page templates in plain HTML, CSS and ES modules.

docs.site: src/index.html (documentation website, generated; serve over HTTP)

components.name: Site footer
components.description: Footer with brand blurb, grouped link columns and a bottom bar.
components.accessibility: Each link group is a <nav> labelled by its heading, so screen reader users can tell the navigation landmarks apart.

components.name: Site header
components.description: Sticky header with brand, primary navigation and actions. On small screens the menu collapses behind a disclosure button.
components.accessibility: The toggle ships with the hidden attribute and is revealed by JavaScript, so without JS the full menu is always visible. The toggle exposes aria-expanded and aria-controls; Escape closes the menu and returns focus. Mark the current page link with aria-current="page".

components.name: Breadcrumb
components.description: Hierarchical trail of links to the current page.
components.accessibility: A <nav> labelled "Breadcrumb" containing an ordered list. Separators are CSS-generated so they are not announced. The current page is marked with aria-current="page".

components.name: Pagination
components.description: Page links with previous/next controls.
components.accessibility: A <nav> labelled "Pagination". Numbers include visually hidden "Page" text, the current page uses aria-current="page", and an unavailable previous/next link has no href so it is removed from the tab order.

components.name: Tabs
components.description: WAI-ARIA tabs with automatic activation. Without JavaScript every panel is shown in sequence with its own heading.
components.accessibility: Roles (tablist, tab, tabpanel), aria-selected, aria-controls and roving tabindex are applied by the script. Arrow keys move between tabs, Home/End jump to the ends; only the active tab is in the Tab order.

components.name: Button
components.description: Primary, secondary, ghost and danger buttons in three sizes, plus icon-only buttons. The same classes style <button> and <a>.
components.accessibility: Use <button type="button"> for actions and <a href> for navigation. Icon-only buttons need an accessible name (visually hidden text or aria-label). Minimum target size is 44×44 px. Disabled state uses the native disabled attribute; use aria-disabled="true" on links.

components.name: Accordion
components.description: Collapsible sections built on native <details> and <summary>. Siblings that share a name attribute behave exclusively (one open at a time) in supporting browsers.
components.accessibility: Native elements provide keyboard support (Enter/Space), expanded state and no-JS behaviour for free. Do not put interactive elements inside <summary>.

components.name: Card
components.description: Content card with optional media, stretched link and footer actions. Each card is a size container, so its layout switches to side-by-side when the card itself is wide (container query), wherever it is placed.
components.accessibility: The stretched link makes the whole card clickable while only the title link is announced and tabbable. Decorative images use alt="". Controls in the footer stay independently clickable.

components.name: Form fields
components.description: Labelled text input, select, textarea, checkbox and radio group with hints and inline errors. Add data-validate to the form for accessible client-side validation.
components.accessibility: Every control has a visible <label>. Hints and errors are linked with aria-describedby; invalid fields get aria-invalid="true" and focus moves to the first error on submit. Group related radios and checkboxes in a <fieldset> with a <legend>. Use autocomplete tokens (WCAG 1.3.5).

components.name: Alert and badge
components.description: Inline status messages in four variants, and compact badges for labels and counts.
components.accessibility: Status is never conveyed by colour alone: each alert has an icon and a text title. For messages inserted dynamically, put them inside a live region (role="status" for polite, role="alert" for urgent). Badges that carry meaning include full text for screen readers.

components.name: Toast
components.description: Transient notifications announced through a polite live region. Trigger declaratively with data-toast or call showToast() from JavaScript.
components.accessibility: Toasts pause while hovered or focused and include a dismiss button (WCAG 2.2.1). Never put the only copy of important information or required actions in a toast. Messages are inserted with textContent.

components.name: Dialog
components.description: Modal dialog on the native <dialog> element, opened and closed declaratively with HTML Invoker Commands (commandfor / command). closedby="any" enables light dismiss.
components.accessibility: showModal() traps focus, makes the page inert, closes on Escape and returns focus to the trigger natively. Label the dialog with aria-labelledby pointing at its heading. Every dialog needs a visible close control.

components.name: Charts
components.description: Vector (SVG) line, area, bar, stacked bar, horizontal bar, donut and sparkline charts drawn from JSON — a file, your API or inline data — with tooltips, keyboard exploration, toggleable series and an automatic data table.
components.accessibility: The SVG is decorative; each chart gets a generated text summary, a focusable region where arrow keys move between data points (announced through a live region), legend buttons with aria-pressed, and a full data table in a details element. Line series also differ by dash pattern, so colour is never the only cue.

components.name: Data grid
components.description: Table rendered from JSON with search, filters, sortable columns, pagination, CSV export and row actions. Server-rendered rows show until data loads, and the toolbar submits as a normal form without JavaScript.
components.accessibility: Sortable headers are buttons with aria-sort; result counts, sorting and paging are announced; action buttons include the row id in their accessible name; the scroll wrapper is a labelled, focusable region. Status is shown as text badges, not colour alone.

components.name: Data table
components.description: Responsive table in a scrollable, keyboard-focusable region. Add data-sortable for sortable columns and data-chart to draw proportional bars behind data-value cells.
components.accessibility: Always include a <caption> and scope on header cells. The scroll wrapper is a labelled region with tabindex="0" so keyboard users can scroll it. Sortable headers become buttons; the sorted column gets aria-sort and the change is announced.

components.name: AI chat
components.description: Embeddable assistant panel with streaming replies, Markdown and code blocks, tool-call steps, inline charts, sources, follow-up suggestions, message actions (copy, regenerate, feedback) and saved history. Connect any model or agent backend with data-chat-endpoint (NDJSON, SSE or text streams) or registerTransport().
components.accessibility: The conversation is a labelled, focusable role="log" region. Replies are announced once when complete (not token by token) and tool steps are announced as they run. Enter sends, Shift+Enter adds a line, Escape stops generation. Every control has a text label; all model output is rendered with textContent, never innerHTML.

components.name: Chat messages
components.description: Static anatomy of chat messages for server-rendered transcripts or custom renderers: user bubble, assistant reply with Markdown, a code block, a tool-call step, sources, a typing indicator and message actions.
components.accessibility: Each message starts with visually hidden "You said" / "Assistant said" text so screen reader users know who is speaking. Tool steps are native details/summary elements. Action buttons have text labels; feedback buttons use aria-pressed.

components.name: Chat widget
components.description: Floating "Ask AI" launcher that opens a support assistant panel on any page. The support persona tracks orders, explains returns and shipping and hands off to a person; swap in your own agent with data-chat-endpoint.
components.accessibility: The launcher is a disclosure button (aria-expanded, aria-controls) that ships hidden until JavaScript runs. Opening moves focus to the message field; Escape or the minimise button closes the panel and returns focus to the launcher. On small screens the panel becomes full-screen.

components.name: Theme customizer
components.description: Drawer for choosing light/dark/system mode, a brand preset or any custom brand colour, density and corner radius. Changes apply live, persist per visitor, report WCAG contrast and generate CSS you can paste into brand.css.
components.accessibility: Native radio groups in labelled fieldsets; the panel is a modal <dialog> (focus contained, Escape closes, focus returns to the trigger). Contrast results are announced through a status message. Custom colours are adjusted automatically until text meets 4.5:1. The trigger ships hidden because it needs JavaScript.

components.name: Theme toggle
components.description: Switches between light and dark themes. Follows the operating-system preference until the user chooses, then remembers the choice.
components.accessibility: A toggle button with a constant accessible name ("Dark theme") and aria-pressed for state. Hidden until JavaScript runs, because it cannot work without it.

blocks.name: Hero centered
blocks.description: Centered hero with soft colour glows, announcement pill, display headline, two calls to action, a short checklist and a large framed product mock below.
blocks.accessibility: The page h1. The checklist is a real list; the product mock is a single role="img" with a description.

blocks.name: Hero split
blocks.description: Two-column hero: announcement pill, display headline with a gradient phrase, lead, two calls to action and a trust row, beside a product mock with floating stat cards. Stacks on small screens.
blocks.accessibility: The page h1. The product mock is one role="img" with a text description; floating cards are decorative duplicates of that description and hidden from small screens. Avatars are decorative initials next to a text rating.

blocks.name: Logo cloud
blocks.description: A row of customer logos with a short heading. Logos are icon-and-wordmark pairs that wrap on small screens.
blocks.accessibility: Each logo is a list item with the company name as text, so screen readers announce the names; icons are decorative.

blocks.name: Stats band
blocks.description: Dark band with a short statement and four large figures. Uses the inverse theme, which stays readable in light and dark mode.
blocks.accessibility: Figures are a description list (dd value, dt label) so each number is announced with its meaning.

blocks.name: Testimonials
blocks.description: Masonry wall of customer quotes with one featured quote on the brand gradient. One column on phones, up to three on desktop.
blocks.accessibility: Each quote is a figure with blockquote and figcaption, so the author is associated with the quote. Avatars are decorative initials.

blocks.name: Feature bento
blocks.description: Bento grid of features in mixed sizes (wide, tall and standard cells) with small visuals: a token swatch row, an accessibility score meter, a code peek and framework chips. Collapses to one or two columns.
blocks.accessibility: Each cell is a list item with an h3. Visuals are decorative (aria-hidden) except the meter values, which are also given as text.

blocks.name: Feature grid
blocks.description: Three-column grid of features, each with an icon, title and one sentence. Columns adapt to the available width.
blocks.accessibility: A list of features; each title is an h3 and icons are decorative.

blocks.name: Feature rows
blocks.description: Alternating rows of copy and media: a heading, paragraph, checklist and link beside a framed product visual. Rows swap sides on wide screens and stack on small ones.
blocks.accessibility: Source order is always copy then media, so reading order is the same on every screen size; only the visual order changes on wide screens.

blocks.name: Steps
blocks.description: Numbered three-step process with dashed connectors, for onboarding, "how it works" or checkout explanations.
blocks.accessibility: An ordered list, so the step numbers are announced; the visual numbers come from a CSS counter.

blocks.name: Category tiles
blocks.description: Grid of shop categories with icons and product counts; each tile is one stretched link.
blocks.accessibility: Each tile is a list item with one link (the category name) stretched over the tile, so it is one tab stop with a clear name; counts are plain text.

blocks.name: Perks
blocks.description: Strip of service promises (shipping, returns, warranty, support) with icons, for store fronts and checkout pages.
blocks.accessibility: A list; icons are decorative and each perk has a bold title and description.

blocks.name: Pricing
blocks.description: Three pricing plans with a monthly/yearly toggle (CSS only, via :has()), a highlighted plan and feature checklists. Browsers without :has() show monthly prices and no toggle.
blocks.accessibility: The billing toggle is a fieldset of native radio buttons with a legend; prices are text. Each plan is a list item with an h3, and the featured plan is marked with a visible text badge, not colour alone.

blocks.name: Promo banner
blocks.description: Store hero: a dark promotional banner with eyebrow, headline, text, two buttons and a product image. Stays dark in both themes.
blocks.accessibility: Use as the page h1 on a store front, or change it to h2 lower on the page. The product image has meaningful alt text.

blocks.name: Blog posts
blocks.description: Latest articles: one featured post with a large image beside a list of compact posts. Each post is a single stretched link.
blocks.accessibility: One link per post (the title) stretched over the card, so each post is a single tab stop announced by its title; images are decorative (alt="").

blocks.name: FAQ
blocks.description: Two-column FAQ: a sticky introduction with a help card on the left and an exclusive accordion on the right. Works without JavaScript.
blocks.accessibility: Native details/summary elements: keyboard and screen reader support come from the browser. The name attribute makes them exclusive where supported.

blocks.name: Team
blocks.description: Team grid with initials portraits on soft gradients, names and roles.
blocks.accessibility: Portraits are decorative initials (aria-hidden); names are h3 headings followed by roles.

blocks.name: Contact
blocks.description: Contact section: contact details on one side and a validated enquiry form in a raised card on the other.
blocks.accessibility: Labelled fields with autocomplete tokens, required markers explained in text, inline errors linked with aria-describedby and focus moved to the first error.

blocks.name: CTA banner
blocks.description: Rounded call-to-action card on the brand gradient with a headline, supporting text and two buttons. Text colour follows the brand preset, so contrast holds for every theme.
blocks.accessibility: Buttons on the gradient use on-brand variants with AA contrast and a matching focus ring colour.

blocks.name: Newsletter
blocks.description: Newsletter sign-up card: heading and promise on one side, a labelled email field and button on the other.
blocks.accessibility: Visible label, autocomplete="email", inline validation errors linked with aria-describedby. Remove data-demo-submit in production.

layouts.name: App shell
layouts.description: Top bar, collapsible sidebar navigation and a scrolling content area. Best for dashboards, admin panels and AI apps.

layouts.name: Centered
layouts.description: A single narrow column. Best for sign in, checkout steps, forms and focused reading.

layouts.name: Docs
layouts.description: Sticky navigation, readable article width and an on-this-page table of contents. Best for documentation, guides and long articles.

layouts.name: Holy grail
layouts.description: Navigation, content and a complementary column. Best for portals, knowledge bases and product catalogues.

layouts.name: Sidebar left
layouts.description: Section navigation beside the content. Best for service pages, help centres and settings.

layouts.name: Sidebar right
layouts.description: Content with a complementary column on the right. Best for blogs, news and article listings.

layouts.name: Split
layouts.description: Two equal columns. Best for contact pages, sign-up with a benefits panel and product details.

layouts.name: Stacked
layouts.description: Full-width sections stacked vertically. Best for home and marketing pages.

pages.title: Services — Acme Studio

skills.name: add-component
skills.description: Step-by-step procedure for adding a new UI component to this repository (snippet, CSS, optional JS module, docs, tests) so it follows the zero-dependency, accessibility and CSP rules. Use when asked to create, add or port a component.

skills.name: audit-a11y
skills.description: Audit accessibility (WCAG 2.2 AA) of this repository's pages and components - static checks for names, labels, ARIA, headings and landmarks, colour contrast of every design token and brand preset in light and dark themes, and Playwright browser checks for keyboard use, focus management, reflow at 320px and the no-JavaScript baseline. Use after any UI change or when asked whether something is accessible.

skills.name: generate-doc
skills.description: Regenerate everything built from source - the documentation website (src/index.html and src/docs/ with live previews, highlighted code, template anatomy, guides and tokens), docs/COMPONENTS.md, the component gallery, catalog.json for AI agents and the page builder canvas. Use after adding or editing any component, block, layout, template page, design token, icon or docs/*.md guide, or when tests report generated docs are stale.

skills.name: pages
skills.description: Create new pages from the layout library and keep shared headers, footers and navigation identical across pages. Use when asked to add a page or inner page to a template, choose or change a page layout, or after editing any partial in src/layouts/partials.

skills.name: validate-w3c
skills.description: Validate this repository's HTML, CSS and SVG against W3C standards with the Nu HTML Checker, then run the HTML/CSS/JS standards suites. Use before finishing any change to src/, after editing templates, layouts, partials or components, or when asked to check standards compliance.
